name: Conformance: Compensate Unwind
description: RFC 0265 fixture for `v2-compensation-unwind.test.ts`: the condition an unwind exists for, caused by the suite unaided. Three effect nodes run in sequence (`e1` → `e2` → `e3`) and succeed; the last node, `fail` (`core.fail`, the always-fails node `conformance-failure` uses), then fails deterministically, so the run has committed effects and a `node-failure` trigger. Each effect node declares a node-level `compensation` whose inverse is the same reserved type with `inputMapping.inverse: true`, and `settings.compensation` asks for a `reverse-completion` unwind on `node-failure`. `core.conformance.compensable-effect` is a conformance-RESERVED typeId (same pattern as `core.conformance.side-effect`): a host that advertises `compensation` and serves this fixture MUST map it to a node it records on the Layer-2 effect ledger (`GET /runs/{runId}/effects`) as exactly one effect per execution, forward and inverse alike, and MUST run it as the inverse action when its resolved inputs carry `inverse: true`. What the effect does is irrelevant; that it is recorded once per execution is the whole contract. The suite reads the unwind through normative paths only: the event log (`compensation.requested` before `compensation.started`), `GET /runs/{runId}/compensation` (attempts in the order `e3, e2, e1`, the reverse of forward completion) and the effect ledger (three inverse records, none added by a `mode: "replay"` fork). Serving the fixture is OPTIONAL; a host that does not list it in discovery `fixtures[]` is `inapplicable` for every leg.
